# A01-S98: Art automation

Extract from the operator’s source text. Transport metadata, signatures and marked context omitted.

[…]

This short article from this year aligns very well with your points: https://www.lodewijkheylen.be/news/Blog%20Post%20Title%20One-3njc8. 

From an art history perspective, there is also a need for a new exhibition on generative art, since with DL/ML one has left previous frameworks which were very rule-based and conceptualist, in favor of showing societal engagement through automation.

This blog explains very well that development concerning generative literature - and thus also the end of written language (which is a classic trope in poststructuralist theory, but which precisely changes with language models): 

http://thecombedthunderclap.blogspot.com/2020/09/the-rise-of-ai-and-future-of-literature.html.
